title: Spotting Scams
blurb: The tricks behind fake messages and fake deals.
cards: i
How scams work
Scammers create urgency, fear or excitement so you act before you think. They pretend to be banks, delivery firms, friends or people offering prizes.
q
A message says your account closes in 1 hour unless you click a link. What is the red flag?
It mentions your account
The extreme urgency and the link
It is about a bank
It is short
Pressure to act fast is the scammer's main tool.
t
A real bank will never ask you for your full PIN or password.
No genuine bank asks for them, ever. Hang up and call the number on your card.
i
Too good to be true
Guaranteed returns, free money and easy jobs that pay a lot for little work are classic bait. If it sounds amazing, slow down and check independently.
q
Someone online offers to double your money if you send it first. What do you do?
Send a small amount to test
Refuse, it is a scam pattern
Ask for a discount
Tell friends to join
Anyone asking you to send money first for a big return is almost certainly scamming you.
q
You think you have been scammed. What is the best first move?
Hide it out of embarrassment
Contact your bank immediately and stop replying
Send more to get it back
Delete all messages
Speed matters. Banks can sometimes block payments, and keeping the messages helps.
example: A stranger promises to double your money by tonight if you transfer funds now. Guaranteed fast returns and pressure to act are warning signs; pause and verify independently.
